The integration of edge computing with artificial intelligence has revolutionized the field of precision agriculture by enabling real-time data processing and decision-making at the network edge. This technological advancement addresses the critical limitations of traditional cloud-based IoT systems, particularly in remote agricultural environments where internet connectivity is often unreliable or unavailable. Furthermore, the ability to process data locally reduces latency and bandwidth requirements, making it an ideal solution for time-sensitive agricultural applications.

Moreover, the proposed system architecture leverages the computational capabilities of the Raspberry Pi 4, which serves as the primary edge computing node. Additionally, an Arduino Uno microcontroller is employed for analog sensor data acquisition, ensuring seamless integration with various environmental sensors. It is important to note that the system incorporates multiple sensors including soil moisture sensors, temperature sensors, and humidity sensors to comprehensively monitor environmental conditions within the agricultural environment.

In addition, the system utilizes a Random Forest machine learning algorithm for predictive irrigation scheduling. This algorithm analyzes historical sensor data and weather patterns to optimize water usage and improve crop yields. Furthermore, a Convolutional Neural Network is deployed for plant health assessment, analyzing visual data captured by a camera module to detect early signs of disease or nutrient deficiency.

The experimental methodology employed a randomized controlled trial design to ensure statistical validity and minimize confounding variables. The results demonstrated significant improvements in water efficiency and crop health monitoring capabilities. The system achieved high accuracy in predicting optimal irrigation schedules and detecting plant health issues. Moreover, the edge computing approach significantly reduced data transmission requirements and improved system responsiveness.

It is worth noting that the system's performance was validated through comprehensive testing in controlled environmental conditions. The results indicate that the proposed framework effectively addresses the challenges of traditional agricultural monitoring systems. Additionally, the modular architecture allows for easy scalability and adaptation to different farming contexts and crop types.

In conclusion, this research presents a comprehensive framework for precision agriculture that combines edge computing, AI, and IoT technologies. The proposed system offers significant advantages in terms of real-time processing capabilities, reduced latency, and improved resource efficiency. Future work should focus on validating the system in diverse agricultural environments and exploring additional AI models for enhanced crop management capabilities. Furthermore, the integration of additional sensor modalities could provide even more comprehensive environmental monitoring and decision-making support.
